mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financing conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during high-rate periods (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months, labor market slack increases, prompting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as investors anticipate corporate hiring acceleration.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat during such UNRATE declines, or the pattern repeats without positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising HOUST (household spending) above 1200 indicate resilient consumer demand, which predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during high HOUST periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 3% in the prior month signals supply-side weakness, leading to a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO contractions of this magnitude.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously over a 3-month window, the dual inflation and policy tightening signal produces a negative S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL each increase over the past 3 months
regime_hint: Dual inflation and rate hike environment
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such co-movements (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) by over 20,000 in a month predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market absorption accelerates.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during such employment spikes.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (GDP) grows at an annualized rate above 4% for two consecutive quarters, the momentum in economic activity supports a positive S&P 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > +4% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a 1% benchmark during such GDP growth episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in RSAFS (retail sales) by 10% or more over three months indicates weakening retail demand, resulting in a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly average < previous month -10% over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such RSAFS declines.
